verdict: The LEFT-RIGHT odd component is SKY: it rises monotonically WITHIN all three nights (focus is untouched inside a night, so a within-night change on fixed optics can only be sky) and its edge dipole sweeps continuously from +0.436 through zero (aug06/set-03) to -0.385 across the corpus — a sensor-fixed term cannot change sign on the same body/lens/focal.

scope: A ratio cancels what is COMMON, so it measures the CHANGE in sky, not the total — a static sky term cancels into the constant part. hypothesis: Running seqsubsky in its CORRECT domain — on frames already flat-fielded by F0, rather than on raw sky x V frames as the dead --desky did — then restoring each frame's sky level, multiplying back by F0 and restacking, yields a flat F1 with the horizon-fixed sky gradient removed and the true vignetting preserved.
test: Three arms, one knob throughout. (1) Synthetic fixture with KNOWN truth: frames (sky x (1+g) + moving stars) x V, V even-radial so its L/R is 1.0000 by construction. (2) Real frames, live path, aug09/set-05, 100 frames, each arm's F0 control built from the same frames. (3) Downstream: the same lights calibrated with F0 vs F1, differenced with isub in both directions against a deliberately broken guard.

verdict: NULL, and structural rather than a tuning miss. THE ITERATION RECONSTRUCTS WHICHEVER FLAT IT IS HANDED: F1 = F_roundtrip. Dividing by F0 is WHAT REMOVES the gradient from the sky, so in the flat-fielded domain the sky is already flat, the degree-1 plane is a CONSTANT, and imul F0 restores exactly what the division took. The five steps compose to F1 = k*F0 - <P_t - m_t>*F0, and the correction term is zero twice over: P_t - m_t = 0 because the sky is flat there, and <P_t - m_t> = 0 because F0 IS the time-average the per-frame deviations are measured against. A second pass cannot help — the fixed point is reached on the first.
why_the_null_is_a_measurement: The positive-control arms move the same code by 81.7% (fixture, round-trip flat = true V) and 93.4% (real data, round-trip flat = another set's flat) where the scheme moves it 1.7% and 1.2%. The harness demonstrably detects recovery at 48-62x the signal the scheme produces.

instrument: synthetic constant/ramp cards at known values, each operation's SAVED output read back with an independent reader (astropy) rather than trusting siril's own report

measured.offset_clips_at_zero: A uniform 300 ADU card with `offset -500` is written as ALL ZEROS, not -200 — despite `help offset` stating 'In 32-bit mode, no clipping occurs'. Only `offset` clips: `isub` gives -200.0 exactly, and `fmul` reaches 90000 (>65535) fine.
measured.stat_excludes_zeros: A card half 0 / half 400 ADU reports Mean 400.0, Median 400.0, Sigma 0.0, Min 0.0 where the truth is 200/200/200. An all-zero region reports 'Statistics computation failed for channel N (all nil?)'.
measured.stack_clips_negatives: Input frames 99.99% negative produced a 100%-zero stack.
measured.seqsubsky_refuses_negatives: 'Failed to generate background samples for image 0: removing the gradient on negative images is not supported'. Pedestal-free dark-subtracted lights always carry negatives; flat division amplifies them (calibrated aug09/set-05 min -2635 ADU). A constant pedestal cancels exactly out of the operator, since the plane fitted to (C+P) is (plane of C)+P.
measured.calibrate_flat_normalisation: C = R/F * k with k ~ mean(F) (probe: light 1000 ADU, flat mean 0.5 -> 661-1984 ADU against predicted 667-2000).
measured.subsky_leaves_a_pedestal: A 500->800 ADU ramp comes back UNIFORM at 627.00 — the plane is removed, the level is not zeroed.

verdict: offset-clipping and stat-zero-exclusion COMPOUND into a trap that hides its own damage: offset zeroes a frame's negative minority and stat then reports the survivors as clean numbers. This corrupted one real-data run of the iterative-flat experiment (a -56443 ADU offset drove the flat's corners to zero, which read back as 'all nil'), and was caught only by reading saved pixels with an independent reader. Any chain step that must subtract a large constant from signed data uses `isub` of a constant card, never `offset`.
scope: siril 1.4.4 flatpak, this rig, 32-bit float mode.

measured.null_control_interleaved_halves: interleaved halves of aug09/set-01 (249 even frames against 249 odd, both through the same undistort chain and solved the same way): the two products span the same drift, so every star's flux is the average of the SAME sensor positions in both and THE PREDICTED TILT IS EXACTLY ZERO. MEASURED +49.08 +- 4.97% at r=10 px and +50.82 +- 5.65% at r=16 px, 3086 stars, residual 0.0085 mag, chi2/dof 3.74, lever 27.9 px — i.e. an 11.8-sigma reading of a quantity that is zero by construction. THE FLOOR IS 49 PERCENTAGE POINTS, and the formal sigma is meaningless, which is the same lesson --selftest 4a teaches on synthetic data. Note the halves are NOT co-registered: Siril picked a different reference frame for each, leaving -2.37 deg and 103 px between their canvases — which is why the lever did not collapse and the null is a fair test of the live configuration rather than a degenerate one.
measured.discrimination_ratio: the planted-ramp control's discrimination AGAINST THE FLOOR is 0.20x — the Siril imul ramp (edge ratio 1.222184) moves the answer +9.85 points against a measured floor of 49.08, i.e. the planted signal is five times SMALLER than what the instrument reports when the truth is zero. The iterative-flat NULL met 48-62x on this standard. Against the INERT arm the discrimination is total: the uniform card moves every number, and every block pair, by exactly 0.00. Re-running the controls reproduced -54.40% / +9.85 points / recovery 1.2408 to every digit.

verdict: NULL — and the null is the deliverable. The interleaved-halves control reports +49.1 +- 5.0% where the truth is zero, so the FLOOR IS 49 PERCENTAGE POINTS. The instrument itself is sound (planted ramp recovered at 1.24x, uniform card inert); the DATA'S GEOMETRY is what fails: the linear mode is degenerate under translational drift, and for a FIXED camera the atmosphere is sensor-fixed and airmass-shaped exactly like the flat's baked-in sky term, so no sensor-frame star-photometry fit can apportion them. Both blockers are independent and either is fatal.
refutes: that the sky x V object tilt can be sized catalogue-free from the drift (BACKLOG:calibration-evidence's 'test that needs no catalogue'); and that the repo's long-quoted 3.11% / 241 sigma is a verified magnitude — it has no tracked record and is not reproduced.
scope: 12 real light sets, 3 nights, one body/lens/focal, 52 solved sub-stacks. The MECHANISM of the defect (a horizon-fixed gradient cannot drift out of a median of un-registered lights; dividing by a flat that absorbed it tilts the object) is untouched — only its magnitude is unmeasured.

why_it_survives_the_two_registered_block: BLOCKER 1 (geometric): the absolute fit needs per-star M_i and per-block z_j nuisances, which absorb a linear mode EXACTLY under a pure translation. Here it is the SAME star in the SAME photons, so M_i cancels identically and nothing per-star is fitted; the lever becomes the spread of star POSITIONS across the canvas — measured 1603-1670 px against the absolute measurement's 29.1 px median. BLOCKER 2 (physical): identical frames carry identical extinction and identical skyglow at every sensor position, so the sensor-fixed atmosphere cancels in the subtraction with everything else the arms share. Executed on the SAME pure-translation panel that killed the absolute design (object_tilt --selftest 4a): the absolute fit returns -0.0464 +- 0.0001 with the lever collapsed to 0.00 px where the differential returns +0.0999 +- 0.0001 with a 1548 px lever.

controls.1_identity_floor: arm A rebuilt with the same flat: every dipole EXACTLY 0.0000 in all three channels, star differential EXACTLY 0.000% at both apertures (n = 920, residual 0.0000 mag), and the two arms are bit-identical in pixels. A TRUE zero, not a small number.

MECHANISM EXPOSED: Siril `calibrate` normalizes the flat by its own level, so a flat's absolute LEVEL cannot reach the product at all; the 5% survives only as 1e-7 float rounding. What reaches the object is precisely the flats' relative SHAPE.

Delivered +0.1547 green (+0.1545 R, +0.1546 B — achromatic, as a synthetic card must be), recovery 97.7%; star differential +16.693% +- 0.014% (r10) and +16.702% (r16). SIGN POSITIVE, opposite to the real signal, so no sign-blind artefact can fake it. Cross-axis leak: dipole_y -0.0010 against dipole_x +0.1547, i.e. 0.6%.

the_two_instruments_disagree_by_1.34_per: compared on the only currency both measure directly, the edge-to-edge RATIO right/left at the pixel instrument's box centres: pixel 0.78920, star 0.77863 (r10) / 0.77890 (r16), a 1.34% difference. NOT an instrument fault: the delivered field's x-slope varies with y. The corner-anchored dipole reads the top and bottom edges, the star fit is a plane over stars spread across the canvas, and a 9-box profile along the MIDLINE reads 0.7683 — the star value sits between them. Measured non-linearity along that midline: max departure from the end-to-end straight line 0.0204. On the PLANTED card — an exactly linear, achromatic field — the same two instruments agree to 0.32% and the profile is straight to 0.0009. The disagreement tracks the field's structure, not the instruments.
normalization_absorption: ON THE OBJECT: -22.477% at -nonorm against -22.550% at the production -norm=addscale -output_norm — the shipped chain absorbs 0.3% of the difference, i.e. essentially none. Pre-registered prediction was < 10%, on the reasoning that a per-frame scalar removes only the ratio field's per-frame constant. HELD. ON THE BACKGROUND: the pixel dipole moves -0.2356 -> -0.3501 (+48.6%) and the channels split (R -0.5025, B -0.3663) where -nonorm holds them together. That is a PEDESTAL ARTEFACT, not imprint: psf's local annulus removes an additive term and regional medians cannot. PROOF, measured on the arms' own levels: An/A is a UNIFORM 2.02x (2.0117 / 2.0231 / 2.0231 / 2.0165 / 2.0215 at TL/TR/BL/BR/centre) while Bn/B runs 1.859 / 1.664 / 1.881 / 1.667 / 1.775 — the counterfactual arm's frames carry an imprint that slides with the drift, so their own statistics vary with frame and addscale's per-frame coefficients become position-dependent. READ THE PIXEL FIELD ON -nonorm ARMS ONLY.
verdict: WIN. A flat-to-flat difference of 0.2851 in edge dipole delivers a 22.5% object-flux tilt across the delivered field, and the delivered imprint field IS the flats' ratio field over the same window (98.9-100.6%, 101.2% after the planted control's own systematic). The transfer from flat shape to delivered object tilt is ~1:1 with no measurable attenuation.
scope: This is the DIFFERENCE of two imprints. It gives the delivered sensitivity to a KNOWN dose difference — the number a corrective needs — and it does NOT give the absolute object tilt, because a ratio cancels what the two flats have in COMMON. It cannot resurrect the 3.11% / 241 sigma figure, which stays UNVERIFIED, and it says nothing about the flat's share of the TOTAL defect, which stays UNTESTED per the registry. What it does establish: any future measurement of a flat's absolute sky content converts to an object tilt essentially 1:1, and the T/B attribution caveat (neither axis isolates the instrument) is untouched by it.
